english.title: Remote pilot of unmanned aircraft fail to provide evidence of compliance upon request
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..),

(A)_[being]_
(B)_[having been]_

a remote pilot of an unmanned aircraft for a flight, failed to comply with a requirement imposed by a constable under paragraph 1 of Schedule 9 to the Air Traffic Management and Unmanned Aircraft Act 2021 to provide evidence of your compliance, as respects that aircraft and flight, with a relevant competency requirement which was applicable as respects you, the aircraft and the flight
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph 1(4) and (5) of Schedule 9 to the Air Traffic Management and Unmanned Aircraft Act 2021.

english.notes:
(i) Paragraph 10 of Schedule 9 to the Air Traffic Management and Unmanned Aircraft Act 2021 provides a defence to this offence.
(ii) Schedule 1 to the Air Navigation Order 2016 provides the meaning of 'remote pilot' and 'unmanned aircraft'.
(iii) Article 3 of the ANO 2016 provides the meaning of 'flight'.
(iv) 'Relevant competency requirement' means a requirement imposed by, or referred to in, any of the following provisions of the ANO 2016 -
(a) article 265B(5)(b) (open category: having the appropriate competency in the intended sub-category of flight);
(b) article 265B(5)(c) (open category: carrying proof of competency);
(c) article 265B(7)(b) (specific category: having the appropriate competency);
(d) article 265B(7)(c) (specific category: carrying proof of competency);
(e) article 265B(8) (specific category: having the appropriate competency specified in the authorisation relating to the flight);
(f) article 265E(2)(b)(ii) (tethered small unmanned aircraft of 250g or more: competency).
(v) The 'NPCC Counter Drones Team' supports and co-ordinates counter drones activity across UK policing. For advice and support from this team, please email Drones.Secretariat@met.police.uk.
